Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a markedly smaller right hemithorax with reduced vascular markings (oligemia) compared to the left, and the CT confirms calcification/occlusion of the right pulmonary artery. In Takayasu arteritis, this indicates chronic obstruction of the right pulmonary artery leading to hypoplasia and volume loss of the right lung.
